notes:
Level tests as formulas instead of hand-written tables

The road to a RISC-V CPU needs about a hundred more levels, many of them
with 8- to 32-bit numbers: truth tables by hand do not scale (a 4-bit
adder was already 256 rows). The new check kind "calc" takes formulas
like S = A + B over numbers made of the A0, A1 ... parts, tries every case
up to 10 input bits and random ones beyond, and checks circuits with
memory through a state and its next-state formula. Formulas are a safe
subset of Python expressions; a level with a bad one is refused on load.

Six levels now use it as a proof; their files shrink by 15,000 lines.
